descriptionChirho: To slaughter or kill an animal, typically in a ritual or sacrificial context, encompassing all Qal active finite forms, infinitives, and the infinitive absolute.
To be slaughtered, used in the Nifal stem to express the passive — the animal or victim is the grammatical subject receiving the action of slaughter.
Qal passive participle used adjectivally or substantivally to describe something that has been slaughtered, functioning as a modifier or noun.
Qal active participle used substantivally to denote the agent — the person who performs the act of slaughtering.
A transferred or contextually distinct use where the participle is applied to a sharp instrument suited for slaughter rather than to the act itself.
